principles.text: No shorts into a gap-down; sit out and wait for a (weak) bounce into declining MAs for the next short entry.
Plan to size up ('huge shorts') on memory names only if the bounce is weak and breadth keeps declining / softwares fail their gap-up.
Don't cover shorts just because the index is extended from the 9 EMA; hold for the longer-term move and use bounces for new entries.
A clean weekly breakout close followed by a gap down below the weekly 9 is a standard fake-out / upthrust that destroys the technicals.
Trade what you see, no bias: a name can either make a lower low in the downtrend or find support on the rising 9/21 and set up an uptrend - let the reaction decide.
Wait for the fake-out to happen before shorting; entering a few days to a week early leads to death by a thousand cuts.
A tight stop (not at the high of day) is a tradeoff: you will get taken out and miss some of the runs/gap downs.
No semi longs while the sector shows relative weakness; if buying leaders on a pullback, softwares are the better candidates.
When nothing is interesting, stop watching the screen - staring leads to overtrading and random trades.
